subject: Clarifying boundary expectations for Dedicated vs Private VPC deployment
messages:
From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@clearhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: deployment guardrails we discussed

Hi Marta —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap of what I heard and a couple of clarifying questions so we can map the right path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) for ClearHealth. I want to make sure we capture the non-negotiables from your privacy and infra teams.

What I heard as requirements:
- Data residency: PHI must remain in your AWS account or a fully isolated tenant in our private offering.
- Strong separation: compute and storage used for ClearHealth cannot be co-tenanted with other customers.
- Key control: customer-managed KMS is preferred, and any service-side keys must be optional.
- Auditability: full request logs, token-level tracing, and 1 year of immutable audit logs.
- Egress controls: explicit deny of external network egress to non-approved endpoints.

Questions for you (short bullets so your folks can answer quickly):
1) Which of the above are absolute must-haves vs. negotiable for the first 6 months?
2) For KMS, is BYOK with a KMS in your VPC mandatory or will a Dedicated option with customer-managed keys in a Redwood-hosted HSM suffice?
3) If we propose a Dedicated pool that is single-tenant compute but with Redwood control plane in our VPC, will that meet your compliance team or do you require the entire control plane inside your VPC (Private)?

Next steps I propose:
- You share the security contact for a short intake call (15–20m) to validate the list above.
- We'll attach a brief checklist and a data-flow graphic so your infra team can quickly mark items as pass/fail.

I've attached a one-page checklist and a diagram of the typical data paths for both Dedicated and Private deployments to help frame the controls matrix.

Thanks — aiming to get this narrowed before we draft a formal Mutual Action Plan.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: clearhealth-map-of-data-flows.pdf, redwood-dedicated-vs-vpc-checklist.xlsx
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@clearhealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: PrivacyOps Team <privacyops@clearhealth.com>
Date: 2027-10-03T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: deployment guardrails we discussed

Hi Kimberly —

Appreciate the concise recap. This matches our notes. Quick answers while I loop in the infosec lead:

- Residency and separation are absolute musts. For the first phase we cannot share compute with other customers.
- BYOK to our AWS KMS is our preference, but we could consider Redwood-hosted HSM if we can retain key lifecycle controls and exportable audit evidence.
- Control plane: our preference is a Private deployment (control plane in our VPC). We can accept a Dedicated model only if the control plane residency and network egress controls meet our policy (i.e., no outbound control plane connections that expose metadata).

I'll put forward two owners for the intake call: Javier Ortega (Infra) and Priya Natarajan (Security). Can they meet tomorrow morning (US PST) for 20 minutes?

-Marta
Senior PM, Data Platforms
ClearHealth
From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@clearhealth.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-03T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: deployment guardrails we discussed

Thanks Marta — this is very helpful and clear. To reduce back-and-forth on the intake call, I pulled together specific artifacts the team typically asks for and what we can provide immediately:

Artifacts Redwood can provide within 48 hours: 
- Dedicated: architecture diagram showing single-tenant GPU pools, network gating, and where audit logs are shipped.
- Private VPC: sample control-plane deployment manifest and list of required VPC endpoints / security groups.
- KMS options: doc outlining BYOK flows, HSM integration points, and responsibilities matrix.
- SOC2 checklist + sample audit extracts (redacted).

Open items we need ClearHealth to confirm:
- Do you require immutable logs stored in your S3, or is a signed/archived copy from Redwood acceptable?
- Are there any disallowed regions or cloud accounts for compute?

Proposed next steps (I will own the deliverables):
1) Intake call with Javier and Priya (20m) — we can do 10/04 at 09:30 PST.
2) Redwood sends the three artifacts above post-call.
3) Quick mapping session with your infra team to validate VPC endpoints (15m).

Kimberly — if that schedule works, I'll slot the call and drop a calendar invite.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai
From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@clearhealth.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, PrivacyOps Team <privacyops@clearhealth.com>
Date: 2027-10-05T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: deployment guardrails we discussed

Great — thanks all for the quick confirmations. Summary and final asks before the intake call this week: 

Summary of confirmed constraints from ClearHealth:
- No co-tenanted compute for initial phase. Dedicated single-tenant or Private VPC only.
- BYOK preferred; Redwood HSM acceptable with customer key controls documented.
- Prefer control plane inside ClearHealth VPC; Dedicated with special controls could be an interim path.

Final asks before 10/04 09:30 PST intake: 
- Marta/Javier/Priya: please upload (even high level) the network egress policy and a short list of required audit fields (e.g., request-id, user-id, model-version, timestamp). This will let Ben tailor the artifact set.
- Ben: please prepare the Dedicated architecture diagram and KMS BYOK flow so the intake call can be a decision-oriented discussion.

I will send the calendar invite for 10/04 09:30 PST and include a short agenda: 1) Confirm must-haves, 2) Decide POC deployment mode, 3) Agree on deliverables & timeline.

If that looks right, we should be able to lock a pilot timeline by end of next week.

Thanks —
Kimberly

Onward.
